method: A Mercator map touches the globe along the equator, where its scale is exact, and stretches every other parallel to the same length as the equator. The parallel on the globe has radius R cos phi while the map draws it with radius R, so the point scale factor is k = 1 / cos phi = sec phi for the absolute latitude phi; because the projection is conformal the meridian scale factor is the same value, which is why angles and small shapes are preserved. The scale error is (k - 1) x 100 percent, the area scale factor is the product of the two equal scales, k squared, so a region at 60 degrees covers four times the map area of the same region on the equator. A 1:N map that is true at the equator reaches 1:(N / k) at that latitude, which the page reports rounded to a whole denominator. The Mercator northing is R ln(tan(45 degrees + phi / 2)) with R = 6378137 m, the sphere radius Web Mercator uses, which equals 0 at the equator and 20037.5 km at the Web Mercator latitude limit of 85.0511287798066 degrees; that limit follows from the square world of the XYZ tile scheme and is the range this page accepts, in both hemispheres. The latitude at which a target scale factor k is reached is arccos(1 / k), reported with a note when it falls beyond the Web Mercator limit. Values are refused outside the latitude limit, a nominal scale from 1:100 to 1:1000000000 and a target factor from 1.01 to 100, and decimal commas are accepted. The page reports the properties of the spherical Mercator only: it does not add the small ellipsoidal correction that keeps Web Mercator from being exactly conformal on WGS 84 coordinates, it assumes the tangent case with the equator as standard parallel rather than a secant Mercator, and it is not a replacement for a projection library. It runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: The Mercator parallel and meridian scale factors are equal and both equal sec phi, so the point scale factor is 1/cos phi: about 1.15 at 30 degrees, 1.41 at 45, 2 at 60, 5.76 at 80 and 11.5 at 85, with an area scale factor of sec squared phi.

Web Mercator is a spherical Mercator that uses the same formulas at every scale, keeps meridians evenly spaced, inflates areas with distance from the equator and is normally cropped near 85 degrees north and south.
